result:
I ran `python -m pytest` once. The result was 2594 passed, 34 failed, 24 skipped and 1 xfailed.

Seven test files contain failing tests:

| File | Failures |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_arguments.py` | 1 (`test_nargs_star`) |
| `tests/test_basic.py` | 1 (`test_basic_functionality`) |
| `tests/test_commands.py` | 1 (`test_other_command_invoke`) |
| `tests/test_context.py` | 1 (`test_ensure_context_objects`) |
| `tests/test_options.py` | 1 (`test_prefixes`) |
| `tests/test_parser.py` | 5 (`test_split_arg_string[...]`) |
| `tests/test_utils/test_echo_via_pager.py` | 24 |

The condensed output listed only the first 10 failures, and neither recovery command returned the rest. I got the full per-file breakdown from pytest's own record of the failed tests, `.pytest_cache/v/cache/lastfailed`, which gave 34 failures in total. I did not run the suite a second time.

I only saw the failure messages for the first 10. I did not see the 24 in `test_echo_via_pager.py`.

`tests/test_chain.py::test_group_chaining` is an expected failure (xfail), not a real failure.

I did not modify any files.
